title: Semantic Retrieval Heads Know What Tokens are Not Important Before Generation
one_line_claim: Identifies semantically-aware attention heads to selectively compress KV cache by detecting important tokens at generation time.
method_summary: CompressKV identifies attention heads within each layer capable of detecting semantically important tokens and their boundary context, then applies layer-adaptive KV cache allocation by analyzing per-layer eviction errors. Rather than using all attention heads uniformly, it selectively retrieves initial, final, and mid-text important tokens.

key_findings.finding: Attention heads have differentiated functionalities for token importance detection.
key_findings.quote: identify the attention heads in each layer that are not only capable of retrieving the initial and final tokens of a prompt, but also capable of retrieving important tokens within the text

key_findings.finding: Layer-adaptive allocation improves on uniform head-based compression.
key_findings.quote: introduce a layer-adaptive KV cache allocation strategy by analyzing cache eviction error at individual layer level

key_findings.finding: Outperforms prior KV compression methods on LongBench and Needle-in-a-Haystack.
key_findings.quote: consistently outperforms state-of-the-art approaches under various memory budgets on LongBench and Needle-in-a-Haystack benchmarks

relation_to_herald.shared: Both address KV-cache compression and its failure modes via per-token signals during generation.
differs_on: CompressKV performs static pre-generation head analysis and allocation; HERALD detects failures dynamically at generation time via per-token logit signals.
CompressKV uses attention head selection to prevent losses; HERALD treats the compressor as a black box and predicts cascading failures.
CompressKV optimizes which compressor to apply; HERALD predicts when any compressor will catastrophically fail.
